topic: Infinitely many solutions: ratio of constants
problem:
In the system of equations below, a and c are constants.
(1/3)x + ay = b
2x + cy = 5d
If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of b/d?

bad.why: There is no data to fit and a, b, c, d are not individually determined, so a regression is unnecessary machinery and underdetermined.
Fitting the coefficient conditions leaves free parameters (only the ratios are fixed), so the fit returns an arbitrary branch.
Four unknown constants make dragging sliders until the lines overlap an absurd setup for one ratio.

algebraFirst.description: Sets up the proportion (1/3)/2 = b/(5d), cross-multiplies to 6b=5d, and solves for b/d; often also tries to find a and c, which are not determined.

explanationNotes: Explain 'infinitely many solutions' as 'both equations are really the same line', so the second equation is the first one multiplied by a single number. Comparing the x-terms shows that number is 2 divided by 1/3, which is 6; it must also turn b into 5d, so 6b=5d and b/d=5/6.
notes: Infinitely-many-solutions means the constants scale by the same factor as the leading coefficients: 2/(1/3)=6, so 5d=6b, giving b/d=5/6. Two arithmetic rows suffice; there is no data to fit, so any regression is unnecessary machinery.
